To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the drag reduction is possible by the use of the grooved surfaces, the magnitude of the drag reduction effect is determined by the length of the laminar layer, and the laminar layer length is determined by the statistical axisymmetry of the flow.
(i) a groove-modified surface can be used to suppress turbulence development in channel flow, and that (ii) the drag reduction effect is preserved at higher Reynolds numbers

the flow over a grooved surface can be made laminar by the suppression of the statistically non-axisymmetric disturbances, which are responsible for the transition and breakdown to the turbulent state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the fundamental understanding of the mechanisms responsible for drag reduction in turbulent flows.
the development of an innovative surface design for drag reduction.
the design of a surface exhibiting maximum drag-reduction effect.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the design of a surface morphology that promotes statistical axisymmetry of the velocity fluctuations can lead to the development of a laminar regime over the entire wetted channel surface and, consequently, to a significant reduction of friction drag.
the proposed grooved surface design is a viable candidate to be applied in the drag reduction of turbulent flows.
, for the first time, a design of the antiturbulence surface is proposed that exhibits a maximum drag reduction effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the surface morphology in the form of grooves aligned with flow direction is a viable candidate for the design of an efficient drag-reducing surface.
the design of the surface morphology for the drag reduction effect can be realized by the suppression of the turbulent flow development.
the design of a surface morphology with a profiled groove is effective in promoting drag reduction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of the antiturbulent surface should be based on the suppression of the statistically axisymmetric flow disturbances.
drag reduction in turbulent flows can be achieved by the early stabilization of laminar flow development with a grooving surface.
a surface exhibiting the maximum drag reduction effect should have a structure that promotes development of statistically axisymmetric disturbances in the flow.
